Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Thompson: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corporation's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mark Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Operating Officer; David Patel, VP of Exploration; Sarah Kline, VP of Marketing; Elena Vasquez, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Raj Singh, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mark Reynolds.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved robust EBITDA growth year-over-year, fueled by higher realized prices and increased production volumes across our integrated portfolio. I'm particularly pleased with our capital allocation priorities, balancing sustainable dividends, opportunistic share buybacks, and disciplined reinvestment in high-return projects. We made strong progress on ESG initiatives, advancing well ahead of our emissions reduction targets. Our capital expenditure guidance emphasizes future spending on profitable opportunities with compelling returns. Lifting costs per BOE continued their downward trend, supported by ongoing cost reduction efforts. Production guidance for the next quarter and full year remains firm, influenced by efficiency gains and regional dynamics. The midstream segment showed impressive performance with rising transportation volumes and key infrastructure advancements. Finally, we bolstered proved reserves additions, achieving a healthy reserve replacement ratio through organic growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to John Ramirez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

John Ramirez: Thank you, Mark. As Mark mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $6.2 billion, up 28% year-over-year. Operating income was $2.1 billion, and net income was $1.5 billion. We generated $2.8 billion in free cash flow and returned $1.6 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $15 billion in debt and $4 billion in cash.

Let me dive deeper into some key financial highlights. Starting with adjusted EBITDA, which came in at $2.6 billion for the quarter, a solid 28% year-over-year increase from last year, building on our trailing twelve-month figure of $9.5 billion, up over 30%. This reflects the resilience of our integrated upstream, midstream, and downstream operations despite OPEC+ cuts and variable global demand. Realized upstream prices averaged $82 per barrel equivalent, up 15% YoY with Brent around $85 amid Middle East tensions and strong driving season demand; U.S. shale benefited from tight WTI-Brent differentials at $4 per barrel, while international hedges covered 70% above $75 floors. Downstream refining cracks widened 22% to $18 per barrel on 3-2-1 basis, with diesel at $25 per barrel from shipping and East Coast exports. Total production rose 12% to 850,000 boe per day, led by Permian growth of 18% to 420,000 boe per day via Phase 3 drilling with 12,000-foot laterals and 2,500 pounds per foot proppant, delivering 1,800 boe per day initial rates, 25% above type curve using slickwater fracs and LWD geosteering; Bakken added 8% to 120,000 boe per day. Midstream throughput jumped 14% to 1.2 million boe per day at 95% utilization, aided by the Matterhorn Express JV with Enterprise Products adding 550 million cubic feet per day takeaway. Costs held firm with $250 million savings, lifting at $8.50 per boe via Apex Digital AI predictive maintenance cutting downtime 22% and LOE 15%, plus 18 super-spec rigs at 650 feet per day. U.S. onshore drove 65% of growth with Permian D&C at $950 per boe, down 10%; international like Guyana Stabroek 15% stake added uplift from Yellowtail FPSO at 250,000 barrels per day gross; North Sea steady with $200 million infill. Offsets included higher Texas taxes up 8% and royalties at 22%, plus refinery turnarounds deferring $50 million. This funds $4.5 billion capex skewed upstream, with net-zero pushes like Permian solar, CCUS, and biofuels. Q4 EBITDA guided $2.5 to $2.7 billion at $80 to $85 Brent.

As we wrap up Q3, our capital allocation framework is central to shareholder value at Apex. With WTI at $78 amid OPEC+ cuts and Asian demand, our $2.8 billion free cash flow up 15% YoY enables three priorities: dividends, buybacks, and reinvestment. On dividends, we hiked the base quarterly by 10% to $0.85 per share, our 17th straight annual increase yielding 4.2% at a 35% payout ratio below peers like Exxon and Chevron at 45%; cash flow breakeven $45 WTI covers 2.2 times at $60 oil with 60% hedging and low-decline shale. Expect 30 to 40% of FCF or $3.2 billion in 2025 dividends at flat prices. Share buybacks accelerated on our undervalued stock at 8.5 times forward P/E versus S&P Energy at 11 times; we repurchased $1.1 billion in Q3 of our $4 billion authorization, retiring 4.2 million shares for 3% EPS boost, YTD $2.9 billion or 8% of float below 10 times EV/EBITDA, with 50% tied to 15% ROCE hurdles like Occidental post-Anadarko but more flexible; plan $2 to $3 billion more in 2025 from FCF for 5 to 7% EPS accretion above $70 oil, signaling confidence in $25 billion NAV at $80. Reinvestment takes 45% of FCF or $4.5 billion 2025 capex for 8 to 10% production growth to 850,000 boe per day; Permian drilling down 12% YoY to $450 per lateral foot via Oasis pads with 15,000-foot laterals, 4,000 pounds proppant per foot, and dissolvable diverters on 250,000 acres allocating $2.2 billion for 180 wells at 40% plus IRRs and 10-month paybacks. Diversifying with $800 million Guyana Stabroek Phase 3 FPSO for 2027 first oil under $35 breakeven partnering Exxon/Hess; $500 million Qatar LNG Train 9 via RasGas on 15% YoY global demand surge per IEA from Europe; 10% or $450 million CCUS like Permian hub for 5 million tonnes by 2026 with 45Q credits and blue hydrogen. Oil-price flex: up buybacks/specials at $90 plus, toggle to 60% reinvest at $50 to $60 maintaining dividend; ROCE 18 to 20% over 12% WACC, returned $12 billion since 2022 growing reserves 15% to 4.2 Tcfe; integrated 50% shale/30% offshore/20% gas/LNG beats Conoco bolt-ons or Pioneer purity for mid-teens TSR.

On capital expenditures, we're guiding 2025 to $6.2 to $6.8 billion, up 7% midpoint fully from cash flow at $60 WTI, targeting above 12% hurdle amid $75 WTI/$80 Brent/gas volatility. 2024 at $5.8 billion midpoint: 65% upstream development, 20% exploration/appraisal, 10% maintenance, 5% low-carbon. Permian efficiencies down 15% costs with 12,000-foot multi-laterals. Upstream $4.1 billion: Permian $2.8 billion for 120 wells to 450,000 boe per day at 25 to 30% IRRs/$65 WTI with CO2/polymer EOR; GoM $950 million Anchor/Winterfell for 50,000 boe per day at 18 to 22% IRRs; Guyana $620 million Liza/Payara for 100,000 boe per day 2026 at sub-$30 breakevens. Exploration $1.3 billion: Permian seismic/10 appraisal, Namibia Orange $300 million two wells like Venus for 500 million boe, GoM wildcats with 4D to 35% success. Maintenance/midstream $650 million flat for 98% uptime, Permian gas gathering. Low-carbon $325 million: Permian CCUS 5 million tonnes 2027 with 45Q like Occidental DAC/EOR; SLB Delfi AI. Blended 18 to 22% IRR, 80% payback under 18 months/$65 deck, $2 billion NPV10; $3 to $4 billion FCF $75 WTI funds dividends/buybacks. Mitigate inflation 5 to 7% tubulars with NOV/Halliburton; 50% hedged.

I will now turn the call over to Lisa Chen for an operational update.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, John. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 850,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought our Permian Phase 3 pads online, which are expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives.

Turning to production outlook, Q3 2024 guidance is 315,000 to 325,000 boe per day midpoint 320,000 up 4% from Q2's 308,000 with 68% oil, from 28 gross operated wells TTS: 22 Permian, 6 Eagle Ford. Base declines offset by new volumes; Permian cycle times under 75 days on 12-well pads/12,000-foot laterals/2,500 lbs/ft proppant for 1,200 boe per day IPs 15% YoY like Pioneer/Exxon; Eagle Ford condensate pads at $2.50 Henry Hub; bake in 2,000 boe per day hurricane risk. Full year maintained 330,000 to 350,000 midpoint 340,000 up 10% with 75% Permian, Q4 exit 345,000; $1.8 to $2.0 billion capex 110 wells 60% IRR $70 WTI, high-graded Midland Waha/Delaware Bone Spring; EOR CO2 pilots 200 bbl per day incremental, Halliburton DecisionSpace NPT down 20% adding 5,000 boe per day, Waha Express 95% capture $2.50 realizations. Regional: Permian 240 to 250 Q3/260 to 275 FY 85 wells 25% IP boost; Eagle Ford 45 to 50/50 to 55; Bakken 20 to 22/13 to 15 post-divest; GoM 10 to 13/12 to 15 Thunder Horse. Hedged 60% Q4 $75 floor; risks LOE inflation/Methane regs mitigated. Positioned 12% FCF yield $70 oil, Reeves tuck-in 15,000 boe per day 4 times EV/EBITDAx, LNG tailwinds.

On lifting costs, we've compounded down 14% annually from $12.45 per BOE Q4 2020 peak to $7.82 Q2 2024; YoY Q2 down 11% from $8.78, sequential flat Q1 $7.85 despite inflation. Quarterly trend: Q2 '23 $8.78, Q3 $8.42 Permian workovers, Q4 $8.15 digital Phase 1, Q1 '24 $7.85 offshore, Q2 $7.82 chemicals. Top quartile Permian peers below GoM $11 to 13 average. Permian 65% production $5.67 down from $7.92 pad scale Delaware electric fracs like EOG; Eagle Ford $8.14 Jonah synergies; GoM $12.45 down 18% ROV drones fixed Oceaneering. Initiatives $250 million 25 to 30% ROI: AspenTech HYSYS AI 17% downtime cut $18 million ESPs, Halliburton Q4 autonomous; Nalco demulsifiers $0.85/BOE/24%, 92% water recycle Gradiant $0.42/BOE; recompletions Baker GeoForm 2.5x payout NPV10x; supply chain 12 to 15% discounts Hi-Crush, labor 9% cut camps. De-risks $35 half-cycle, opex 18% revenue; $7.00 by '25 Jonah/automation, 60% plus FCF return 8 to 10% growth.

Midstream added resilient EBITDA: Q3 $620 million up 12% YoY 5% sequential, 42% total; transportation 2.8 million bbl per day crude up 9% Permian 1.9 million 15% Pioneer/Oxy anchors 85% take-or-pay WTI Midland $2.50 contango; gas 4.2 Bcf per day 7% Haynesville 1.8 Bcf 18% Plaquemines LNG $0.25 premium; NGL 850,000 bbl per day 6% Mont Belvieu $0.35/gal Dow/Exxon; 92% utilization 18,000 miles $1.12/bbl crude $0.28/Dth $285 million revenue record. Permian 55% EBITDA Haynesville/Eagle Ford 25% Bakken 12%; Houston docks 450,000 bbl per day exports Brent $82. Infrastructure $1.2 billion 65% in service: Gray Oak 200,000 bbl per day JV ONEOK/Plains $250 million 10-year take-or-pay 110% FERC 12 to 14% IRR; Matterhorn Phase II 550 MMcf/d Permian Waha FID Q4 Exxon/EQT AI Halliburton 22% downtime; Mont Belvieu III 125,000 bbl per day Enterprise 95%. 40% electric/solar 25% emissions cut EPA/ESG LPs; 92% fee-based 2.3x coverage EnergyFlow MLP $500 million notes 5.25%; Q4 $640 to 660 million 8 to 10% 2025 growth Permian 7 million/LNG 14 Bcf/d; FERC risks offset STRATOS CCUS.

Now I will turn it over to David Patel for an update on our exploration activities.

David Patel: Thank you, Lisa. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Delaware Basin and are planning to drill 180 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

On proved reserves, we hit a total replacement ratio of 142% for 2023, fifth straight year over 100% three-year average 128% beating peer 110% Wood Mackenzie; organic 115% excluding M&A. Additions 158 million BOE up 12% YoY to year-end 2.4 billion BOE up 6% 65% liquids 45% PDP. Sources: extensions/discoveries 92 million 58%, revisions 38 million up 25% longer laterals/fracs, acquisitions 28 million Permian bolt-ons; versus 111 million production 304,000 boe per day up 8%. U.S. onshore 78% organic: Permian 65 million 132% RRR Factory SIMOPS 12 pads 12,000-foot/55-stage slickwater 1.2 million BOE EUR 15% up EOG F&D $8.50/BOE half basin; Eagle Ford 22 million 108% Black Hawk geo/fiber 7-day cycles 20% proppant; GoM 15 million Highlander 5,000 net Chevron Anchor 4D; Brazil Santos 8 million Petrobras 2026. $250 million subsurface ApexAI ML 50TB data 85% sweet spots up from 72% exploratory success 65% up 28%; 15,000-foot laterals diverters 9-month payout $60 WTI. Fortifies returns 65% Tier 1 50% IRR strips 5 to 7% growth 2028 no equity, 50% FCF buybacks/dividends Pioneer-style; 2024 organic 120% plus Permian stack/skid GOM.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Sarah Kline to discuss our marketing strategy.

Sarah Kline: Thank you, David. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for NGLs in the Gulf Coast and Asia markets, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact on realizations and export volumes is significant, leveraging infrastructure like Mont Belvieu and LNG ramps for premium pricing amid petrochemical and energy transition demand.

I will now turn it over to Elena Vasquez to discuss our sustainability efforts.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Sarah. We are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and operating in a sustainable manner. We have made significant progress on reducing our greenhouse gas emissions, targeting 40% Scope 1 and 2 intensity cut by 2030 from 2019's 18.2 kg CO2e per boe, accelerating ahead. YTD Q3 absolute emissions down 17% to 4.2 million metric tons from 5.1 million; intensity 22% lower to 14.1 kg below 15.5 milestone. Methane top priority down 28% to 0.18% OGMP 2.0 Level 4+; Permian 1.2 million acres BHGE Luna 85% sites satellite/drone 35% venting cut 1.2 Bcf recovered $8 million. Flaring 0.8% down 42% from 1.4%; U.S. shale 62% rig electrification Caterpillar microgrids 45% diesel cut; North Sea NORSOK FGRUs Troll 95% recovery 120,000 tons. CCUS scaling: Permian Oxy hub 1 million tons Q2 Denbury Class VI $45 million 45Q; ADNOC blue H2 200,000 tons 2026 Honeywell. North America 75% 25% drop electrification/AI completions 20% less proppant/water NOx/VOCs; Europe/offshore 19% Equinor Hywind 15% power; Middle East/Africa 12% reforming upgrades geopolitics Q4 catch-up. $120 million opex savings YTD 3:1 ROI $450 million ESG capex over Conoco 2.5:1; SEC TCFD/EU CBAM compliant Sustainalytics 78/100 $2 billion BlackRock; Scope 3 85% 15% cut methane credits/renewable diesel First Movers; net-zero 2050 ERM assured. Turns ESG value driver Brent $78 Henry volatility.

I will now turn the call over to Raj Singh to discuss our technology initiatives.

Raj Singh: Thank you, Elena. We are leveraging technology to improve our operational efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance safety. We are investing in automation, data analytics, and artificial intelligence to optimize our operations, including AI reservoir models and predictive maintenance across rigs and wells. We are also exploring new technologies such as carbon capture and storage, with pilots integrating Delfi platforms and machine learning for geosteering and completions, cutting NPT and boosting EURs while supporting CCUS hubs.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your lifting costs per BOE. You've guided to another quarter of improvement—could you walk us through the trend analysis and the key cost reduction initiatives behind it, with some color by basin?

John Ramirez: Absolutely, Sarah, great question. Lifting costs—or LOE per BOE excluding capex and DD&A—are core to our efficiency. Company-wide down from $12.45 per BOE Q4 2020 to $7.82 Q2 this year, 14% CAGR; Q2 '24 down 11% YoY from $8.78, flat sequential Q1 $7.85. Trend: Q2 '23 $8.78 baseline, Q3 $8.42 Permian workovers, Q4 $8.15 digital, Q1 '24 $7.85 offshore, Q2 $7.82 chemicals—top quartile Permian peers below GoM $11-13. Permian $5.67 from $7.92 pad Delaware electric like EOG; Eagle Ford $8.14 Jonah upside; GoM $12.45 down 18% drones Oceaneering. Digital AspenTech/Halliburton AI 17% downtime $18 million; Nalco $0.85/BOE 24%, Gradiant 92% recycle $0.42; Baker recompletions NPV10x; Hi-Crush discounts labor 9%. De-risks $35 breakeven opex 18% revenue; $7.00 '25. Granularity enough?

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Torres with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Torres: Good morning. What are your expectations for production guidance next quarter and full year, including key factors?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Mike. As detailed, Q3 315k-325k boe/d up 4% sequential on Permian/Eagle Ford TTS, Permian efficiencies 75-day cycles 1,200 IP30s; FY 330k-350k 10% growth Permian-led, capex funds 110 wells high-IRR inventory EOR/digital/midstream; regional breakdowns hold, hedged resilient to hurricanes/macro. High end feasible.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Rao with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Rao: Could you please provide more color on EBITDA drivers and YoY changes?

John Ramirez: Sure, Emily. Q3 $2.6B up 28% on $82 realizations 15% lift Brent $85, cracks $18 diesel $25, volumes 850k Permian 420k 18% Phase 3, midstream 1.2M 14%, costs flat $8.50 AI savings; U.S./intl balanced offsets taxes/turnarounds. Q4 $2.5-2.7B.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Hale with BMO Capital. Please go ahead.

Tom Hale: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

David Patel: Thanks, Tom. Our Permian Delaware seismic and 180-well plan build on 142% RRR organic 115% 158M BOE adds to 2.4B reserves; extends 15+ year inventory Tier 1 Permian/Eagle Ford/GoM/Brazil high-grading via ApexAI 85% hits, supports 5-7% growth FCF returns without dilution, flexes capex to high-IRR amid consolidation.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Kim with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Laura Kim: What is the outlook for NGLs and midstream products in the coming years?

Sarah Kline: Good morning, Laura. Strong with Permian/Haynesville ramps, 850k NGL/LNG demand Asia/Europe premiums $0.35/gal ethane Gulf exports; infrastructure Gray Oak/Matterhorn/Mont Belvieu III 8-10% volume growth 2025 92% utilization fee-based, de-risks realizations CCUS transport upside.

Operator: Our next question comes from Chris Lang with RBC. Please go ahead.

Chris Lang: Could you elaborate on your sustainability targets?

Elena Vasquez: Thanks, Chris. 40% Scope 1/2 intensity by 2030 on track YTD 22% to 14.1 kg/boe via methane 0.18% Luna/FGRUs, flaring 0.8%, CCUS 1M tons Permian Oxy/ADNOC H2; regional gains efficiency $120M savings 3:1 ROI compliant regs score 78/100; Scope 3 15% cut net-zero 2050.

Operator: Our next question comes from Dana Patel with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Dana Patel: What are the key technology initiatives you are focused on?

Raj Singh: Good morning, Dana. Automation/data/AI core: predictive maintenance 22% downtime, Delfi geosteering frac opt, ApexAI reservoirs, CCUS integration electric rigs solar; shave drilling 10-15% safety margins boost EURs supports ESG/capex efficiency.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mark Reynolds for closing remarks.

Mark Reynolds: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
